description: SkyPilot multi-cloud LLM serving — sky serve up provisions GPU replicas across AWS/GCP/Azure/Kubernetes, auto-picks cheapest region, handles spot preemption, and load-balances across replicas. vLLM runs the model on each replica behind a managed endpoint.

buildHints.whenToUse: Pick SkyPilot when you need multi-cloud LLM inference, spot-GPU cost savings, or automatic failover across cloud regions. For single-host or single-cloud deployments, use vllm-server or tgi-server directly — SkyPilot adds value only when multi-cloud orchestration or spot preemption handling matters.
firstSteps: Authenticate with at least one cloud: `aws configure` / `gcloud auth login` / `kubectl config` — then run `sky check` to confirm ≥1 cloud is enabled.
Edit service.yaml: set resources.accelerators (e.g. A100:1), envs.MODEL_ID (e.g. meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct), and replicas.
sky serve up -n <endpointName> service.yaml   — pass --env HF_TOKEN=$HF_TOKEN for gated models.
sky serve status <endpointName> — wait for replica READY (3-10 min cold start), then hit the printed endpoint URL.
sky serve down <endpointName> when done — you are billed while replicas run.
gotchas: `sky serve up` starts billing immediately. `sky serve down` is not optional — add a teardown step to any CI/review pipeline.
Accelerator strings are SkyPilot-specific: A100:1, A100-80GB:1, H100:1, L4:1. Cloud instance names (p4d.24xlarge) go under resources.instance_type, not accelerators.
use_spot: true saves 50-80% but spot preemption restarts replicas. Tune readiness_probe.initial_delay_seconds for your model's cold-start time; the default 600s is intentionally conservative.
First `sky serve up` provisions a controller VM (~$30/mo on AWS). Leave it running — it coordinates all your services and restarting it is slower and pricier than keeping it live.
Large model weights re-download on every replica spawn unless you add file_mounts pointing to an S3/GCS bucket. For models >7B parameters, set up weight caching before scaling to multiple replicas.
Kubernetes backend: `sky check kubernetes` must succeed BEFORE `sky serve up` — otherwise SkyPilot silently falls back to the first configured cloud.
architectureNotes: service.yaml is the replica spec — describes what runs on each GPU VM. sky-serve.yaml is the controller config — load-balancer policy, replica scaling, controller sizing. Edit service.yaml first; most teams never touch sky-serve.yaml.

SkyPilot is the orchestrator; vLLM is the default inference engine. Swap the run: block to use TGI, SGLang, Triton, or a custom FastAPI app. SkyPilot only requires an open port and a passing readiness probe.
The readiness probe hits /v1/models. Any OpenAI-compatible server that responds to that path qualifies as ready.

placeholders.description: {{modelId}} — HuggingFace model ID (e.g. meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct). {{acceleratorSpec}} — GPU spec (A100:1, H100:1, L4:1). {{port}} — port the inference server binds to (default 8000).
HF_TOKEN — HuggingFace token for gated models. Copy .env.example to .env and set HF_TOKEN before deploying.
